2026-09-16 (AI-fact-elimination sweep, fin/45, re-examined all 6 remaining unprovenanced facts fact-by-fact, per this task's own standing 'try hard before declaring bespoke' instruction): `apply-recognizers.mjs zack-fair` re-run first (0 new facts, confirms still uncovered). Findings per fact:
1. SOURCE `putCounter` (ETB +1/+1 on self) — re-checked `putCounterSelf-effect-structural.ts` directly: this recognizer ALREADY has a real, whole-pool-vetted, DELIBERATE decline for this exact card (its own module doc comment names Zack Fair by name: real text is "Zack Fair enters WITH a +1/+1 counter on it" — no "put" verb at all, a genuine CR 614.12 replacement-effect idiom, not this recognizer's own "put ... counter on ..." template) — confirmed genuinely bespoke, not a stale/lazy decline.
2. SOURCE `sacrifice` (self, as activation cost) — **real, closable recognizer-lane escalation, found today**: `sacrificeCostNamedType-structural.ts`'s own module doc comment ALREADY names this exact card (plus Blazing Bomb/Instant Ramen/Elven Passage) as a confirmed, real "Sacrifice <named self>/this <type>" cost shape it deliberately declines (its own `\b(a|an)\b` anchor structurally never matches a proper name or "this"). A sibling recognizer (e.g. `sacrificeCostSelf-structural.ts`, same file/discipline as its own sibling) reading `activationCost` for "Sacrifice <self-name>|<short-name-before-comma>|this <type>" (reusing the already-established `selfSubjectAlternation` vocabulary `dies-trigger-structural.ts`/`putCounterSelf-effect-structural.ts` both already share) would produce `{event:'sacrifice', subject:'self', target:'self', annotations:[...]}` — exactly this card's own existing hand-authored fact shape. Checked the other 3 named siblings directly: Elven Passage has the identical fact but still in the OLD pre-v2 schema (zone/sourceText, no annotations) — untouched by this recognizer either way; Blazing Bomb and Instant Ramen currently have NO such fact at all (their own `synergy.json` never declared one) — flagging this discrepancy as context, not fixing it (out of my assigned slugs). Escalating to the recognizer lane.
3+4+6. SOURCE `grantKeyword` (Indestructible, targeted, untilEndOfTurn), SOURCE `putCounter` (+1/+1 targeted, counter-transfer magnitude = self's own live counters), SINK 'wants a creature you control' (shared target pool for all 3 consequences) — all three come from ONE `kind:'custom'` closure. Checked whether a migration to `kind:'program'` (my own lane, no new engine vocab needed for 2 of the 3 actions — `grantKeyword`/`putCounter` `EachAction`s and the `selfCounters` `ValueRef` all already exist) would close any of them: **it would not, today** — `program-ast-walker.ts`'s own `actionOccurrence()` only builds an occurrence for `'destroy'`/`'equip'` `EachAction`s; `'grantKeyword'`/`'putCounter'` are explicitly named in that file's own header as "walked structurally but has no occurrence shape built for it yet." Also checked whether the WHOLE ability (all 3 consequences, one shared target) could migrate atomically: no — the equip-reattach third of it needs a Query source for "equipment currently attached to a given card" (the reverse of `getEquippedBy`), which doesn't exist in `combinator.ts` today (only `creaturesInPlay`/`permanentsInPlay` sources exist). Considered a PARTIAL migration (grantKeyword+putCounter-transfer onto `program`, leaving only equip-reattach as `custom`) but rejected it: splitting one atomic target-choice into two independently-resolving `Effect`s (a `program`'s own `selectUpTo` plus a leftover `custom`'s own separate `chooseTarget` call) would require both to coincidentally re-derive the IDENTICAL creature from the same pool — true today (`chooseTarget`'s pool-exhaustion is deterministic and this ability's own target pool, 'creatures you control excluding self,' doesn't change between the two calls), but a real, fragile, non-obvious invariant to leave sitting in the codebase for a migration that closes ZERO facts today anyway (the walker gap above blocks it regardless of `custom` vs. `program`). Not attempted — recommend deferring the WHOLE ability's migration to one atomic pass once BOTH (a) the walker gains `grantKeyword`/`putCounter`-via-`ApplyToBound` occurrence support (recognizer lane) AND (b) a new Query source for 'equipment attached to self' lands (engine-core lane), rather than migrating piecemeal now for no closure benefit. Left `definition.ts` unchanged.
5. SINK `putCounter` (target self, 'wants its own +1/+1 counters,' the magnitude read) — same root cause as #3/4/6 (opaque `custom` closure reading `ctx.self.getCounters('+1/+1')`); same deferred-atomic-migration recommendation applies, not closable independently of the others.

Conclusion: 1 fact (#1) is genuinely, permanently bespoke (a real English-wording divergence, already correctly declined by a careful existing recognizer). 1 fact (#2) is closable TODAY via a real, already-partially-justified new recognizer (cite above) — escalated. 4 facts (#3/#4/#5/#6) are blocked behind a real two-lane dependency (recognizer walker occurrence support + a new engine-core Query source) and were deliberately NOT force-migrated piecemeal given the zero-benefit/real-risk tradeoff explained above — escalated as a combined future task, not silently left as a shrug.

Migrated to the unified Fact model (2026-09-12). Real oracle: "Zack Fair enters with a +1/+1 counter on it. / {1}, Sacrifice Zack Fair: Target creature you control gains indestructible until end of turn. Put Zack Fair's counters on that creature and attach an Equipment that was attached to Zack Fair to that creature." {W} Legendary Creature — Human Soldier, 0/1 (Scryfall-verified). Annotated (ANNOTATED_CARD_SLUGS), no presence sources, baseline self-cast/self-enters added (previously none), value:-1 placeholders resolved via `compute-weights.mjs --slug=zack-fair` (all 1 — every effect here is single-instance magnitude). 8 facts total (was 5, old id/sourceText/highlight schema): self-cast, self-enters, ETB +1/+1 counter (unchanged modeling — no distinct 'enters with counters' replacement-effect mechanism exists anywhere in this engine, checked state.ts's addCard/move; this is a named onEnter trigger, now with on:'enter' for real 603.6b auto-fire), self-sacrifice-as-cost (bare ACT tag, same shape summon-bahamut's own self-sacrifice fact uses — REPLACES the old, incorrect `{zone:'Graveyard', subject:'self'}` ZoneFact, which wrongly claimed a real guaranteed movement that never actually happens in this engine), grantKeyword Indestructible (targeted:true, untilEndOfTurn:true — the latter is a real, already-existing field, not new here), and a real putCounter counter-TRANSFER onto the target (read Zack Fair's own live count, then place that many on the target — no counter-move primitive exists anywhere in this engine, this read-then-place pair is the correct real mechanism). Two sinks: wants-own-counters (X = counters already on self) and one shared 'creature you control on the battlefield' want (serves all three consequences at once, since the real oracle text targets ONE creature ONCE, not three independent choices).

Equipment re-attachment ('attach an Equipment that was attached to Zack Fair to that creature') is now REAL, executable code (`ctx.self.getEquippedBy()` + `actions.equip`) — an earlier version of definition.ts incorrectly claimed no reverse attached-Equipment lookup existed; `state.ts`'s own `attachedToId`-scan (`getEquippedBy`) was added to this engine after that comment was written and does expose it. Despite being real and executed in the scenario (produces a genuine `fn:'equip'` trace line), it deliberately got NO new synergy Fact — checked real pool precedent first (Weapons Vendor/Beatrix, Loyal General/Raubahn, Bull of Ala Mhigo/Dragoon's Lance all call `actions.equip` for real via a `custom` effect and NONE of them declares an `event:'equip'` produce fact; `equip` is still in verify-synergy.mjs's own PARKED_ACTION_FNS, and the reverse 'explain every action' check explicitly skips parked fns) — adding one here would break an already-established, considered, same-day pool convention for a fourth card, not close a real gap.

Self-sacrifice-as-cost is a REAL, documented, general engine gap this migration surfaced and left open (not fixed): engine.ts's own `unsupportedCostComponent` only recognizes 'Sacrifice another/a/two X' as a payable cost component, never a NAMED self-sacrifice ('Sacrifice Zack Fair') — so `canActivateAbility`/`activateAbility` always reject this exact ability through the real engine, and per that same function's own doc comment this can't be fixed by modeling the sacrifice as a real `{kind:'sacrifice'}` effect either (this card's own logic reads Zack Fair's LIVE counters/attached Equipment, which only stays correct because the sacrifice never actually removes it from the battlefield — genuinely sacrificing it first would need real 608.2h last-known-information tracking, a real, separate, unbuilt gap). Added a new, generalized (not per-card) `isSelfSacrificeActivationCostFact` exemption to verify-synergy.mjs, symmetric to the existing `isSelfTapActivationCostFact`/`isSelfExileActivationCostFact`.

knownGaps: Self-sacrifice-as-cost ('{1}, Sacrifice Zack Fair') is never actually paid/executed by this engine — engine.ts's own unsupportedCostComponent doesn't recognize a NAMED self-sacrifice as a payable cost component, so canActivateAbility/activateAbility always reject this ability for real. Deliberately not fixed (fixing it safely would need real 608.2h last-known-information tracking so this card's own 'read Zack Fair's live counters/attached Equipment' logic stays correct once it's actually gone — a real, separate, unbuilt gap). This card's own scenario fires the ability directly via resolveCard instead of pilotActivate for exactly this reason.

No distinct 'enters with counters' replacement-effect mechanism exists anywhere in this engine — checked state.ts's own addCard/move for an 'arrives pre-loaded with counters' hook; none exists. Zack Fair's own ETB counter stays modeled as a named onEnter trigger calling putCounter, same as every other pool card with 'enters with a counter' text.

No counter-move/transfer primitive exists anywhere in this engine (state.ts's putCounter is purely additive) — the real 'Put Zack Fair's counters on that creature' transfer is modeled as a read of Zack Fair's own live count immediately followed by a real putCounter onto the target, the correct real mechanism available rather than an approximation of a nonexistent one.
